label: yes
controls_available: Drag a visible ingredient jar into the mortar; full-mode grading requires a sampled jar_drag gesture.
Hold the visible pestle and release it; in difficulty 1 the five grind notches advance at 240 ms per notch, capped at the fifth notch.
Click STIR PATH; each click advances the committed path by six of 24 samples, so route motion is agent-triggered.
Click WATER for up to seven 40-pixel moves toward the origin, or BELLOWS for up to six 22-pixel moves along the current heading.
Click SEAL to submit the final position and effect; this is the administrative final submission.
autonomous_processes: During a full-mode pestle hold, requestAnimationFrame repeatedly calls advanceGrinding; elapsed task time changes grindStep by one for each 240 ms interval.
The CSS apoth-pound animation runs while the pestle is held, but it is visual-only and does not affect the grader.
The 1.8-second fresh-failure timeout only removes the failure overlay after a failed submission and is administrative.
There is no autonomous flask/path, water, bellows, or recovery motion: those state changes occur synchronously in stir or utensil handlers.
grouped_control_modes: full jar-drag ingredient load or replacement
full pestle-hold and release grind control
ladle-click STIR PATH progression across all route stages

clause_i.reason: For D = full pestle-hold/release, the generator shuffles the grind-step schedule for the two route commits from five notches, so the required release/continue choice varies across seeds and stages. An observation-free q using only prior mouse actions and task times cannot choose the delayed release action for every C_Delta history because the current ingredient/path and route-ring geometry are visible state, not I_t.

clause_ii.reason: The bounded current screen shows the selected ingredient's path preview, the route-ring center aperture and heading fan, and the current/filled grind notch. With the visible 240 ms tick, a stationary g using that endpoint frame (the configured one-frame, 240 ms window) can predict the notch at delivery and choose pointerup or continued hold.

clause_iii.reason: Use a history while the pestle is held at a required step s<4, positioned 120 ms before its next 240 ms tick; with no pointerup, at tau=120 ms<Delta=240 ms the visible grind state changes from s to s+1. Releasing at H_t makes the route curve match the visible gate, while the same release at H_t^tau makes a different curve that does not advance that route ring, so its route-commit value/advantage is strictly lower. Success remains possible by replacing the active ingredient and regrinding; the loss is the changed grind/path state, not a deadline or mere later submission.

common_visible_process: The common process is full-mode pestle grinding: while the pointer remains down, task time drives visible 240 ms grind ticks, the current notch changes on the track, and the selected ingredient's preview has a different curvature. The same visible state determines whether the delayed release is optimal and makes release at the old notch expire as a route-ring opportunity.

pre_run.reason: No generated instance has a qualifying autonomous outcome phase after preparation: full-mode release itself selects the outcome-affecting grind notch, and every route path advances only through further STIR PATH clicks. Therefore a successful solve cannot start such a phase and send no more outcome-affecting actions; no percentage is invented.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 is three ingredients, two route commits, five grind notches, no vortices, and one bone; full interaction is jar drag plus duration-based pestle control; the observation window is 240 ms with one frame.
Route schedules are shuffled from the available grind steps and the visible gate is required to uniquely identify each ingredient/step choice.
Generated mechanics set grind_tick_ms to 240, path samples to 24, stir_stride to 6, and expose jar/mortar/pestle geometry.
The visible track reflects current grindStep; pointerdown starts grinding, requestAnimationFrame advances it from performance.now in 240 ms ticks, and pointerup records the selected release notch.
The canvas visibly renders the selected path preview and route gate aperture/fan, and the full UI binds jar drag, pestle, STIR PATH, WATER, BELLOWS, and SEAL controls.
Stir and utensil movement are performed synchronously on their input handlers; route progress only increments when a completed path was aligned.
The held-pestle animation is tied to data-grinding, while the current/filled grind track and the tool buttons are visible UI elements.
Task time drives virtual performance time, timers, and animation frames in live windows and freezes them at paused boundaries; this makes the grind timer the relevant live-versus-paused state change.
The independent contract enforces the 240 ms mechanics and replays full-mode pestle start/ticks/release plus path alignment and route progress.

The implementation solver waits for the target grind notch before releasing the full pestle and then advances each path through repeated visible STIR PATH clicks; this is implementation evidence, not private state available to the policy.
